input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full: Vendor expressly defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims (20.1), covering IP infringement/misappropriation by the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud (20.2). Section 20.4 supplies the standard procedure — prompt notice, reasonable cooperation (at the indemnifying Party's expense) and control of the defence, with a settlement-consent protection. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow: unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, plus Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Section 20.5 additionally gives the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder. No super-cap is needed: Section 21.3 treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims, so Vendor's indemnity is uncapped, which is better than the 3× fallback. The absence of the customary Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions from Vendor's IP indemnity is a fallback-only feature and operates in our favour, so no redline is warranted.
